newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokai Kogyo seeks court protection -- media.
newsitem.headline: Tokai Kogyo seeks court protection -- media.

text.p: Japanese construction firm Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd is preparing to apply for court protection from creditors under Japanese law, Japanese media reported on Friday.
Jiji new agency, quoting unnamed sources, reported that the company had debts totalling 520 billion yen.
Jiji and NHK public television reported that the construction firm, listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE), is set to apply for court protection later on Friday.
When a company applies for court protection from creditors under Japanese law, the move is widely regarded as a sign that the company is on the verge of failing.
A company official later told Reuters that its board members were holding a meeting to decide on various issues, including the possible application for court protection.
He said he could not tell when the board members would reach a decision.

Tokai's shares were suspended by the TSE after they fell on the news. Other construction shares such as Tobishima Corp and Aoki Corp also tumbled on the news. Aoki was the largest percentage loser on the exchange.
The media reports also pushed up Japanese government bond prices, traders said.
